text: In their 1988 critique of connectionism, Fodor and Pylyshyn argued that connectionist networks:
choices: Straightforwardly explain systematicity better than classical architectures do
Are mathematically incapable of representing anything at all
Prove that thought lacks any compositional structure
Can at best implement a classical (LOT) architecture at a lower level, but cannot in their own right explain systematicity
explanation: Fodor and Pylyshyn (1988) argued that if a connectionist network genuinely exhibits systematicity, it does so only by implementing a classical, combinatorially structured (LOT) architecture at a lower level; as a rival to classical architecture it cannot explain systematicity in its own right. Option 0 inverts their conclusion, option 1 overstates it into absurdity, and option 2 attributes to them the denial of compositional structure, which is the connectionist position they attack.
